skill.name: education-email-marketing-specialist
skill.description: Plan education email campaigns, program-inquiry capture, enrollment-information journeys and audience segmentation for schools, training providers and courses. Use for marketing and informational journey design, not admissions or student eligibility decisions.
skill.summary: Draft education email campaigns and journey plans with consent checks, audience segmentation, and enrollment-aware exclusions.
skill.author: email-marketing-skills-hub

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 11 requests verification of public platform documentation and account controls before specifying interface steps. It explicitly permits other platforms and requests no host inspection or system enumeration.

Line 24 preserves marketing consent, preferences, and suppression status and prohibits changing status to force delivery. It contains no environment-variable access or configuration-library invocation.
Line 18 limits inquiry capture to program interest and necessary contact information, with safeguards for minors and sensitive data. It requests no system inspection or reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Education email campaigns can confuse program interest, marketing permission, and enrollment status. This skill drafts audience rules, campaign copy, and journey plans that keep those distinctions clear.
actual_capabilities: Draft subject lines, preheaders, concise email bodies, and one primary call to action for program campaigns.
Define audience segments using declared program, intake, study mode, campus, and relationship stage.
Plan inquiry capture with minimal contact fields, separate guardian records, and approved processes for minors.
Specify journey entry events, delays, branches, exits, re-entry rules, deduplication, and uncertain-delivery holds.
Review launch blockers involving consent, stale dates, enrollment updates, recipient mapping, and authorized execution.
Plan measurement using unique-person denominators, matched attribution windows, cohort maturity, and authorized enrollment data.
limitations: Provides instructions and draft deliverables, not a bundled email sender or live platform integration.
Does not decide admissions, scholarship eligibility, or enrollment, and does not guarantee educational or employment outcomes.
Requires approved sources for program facts and current platform documentation for implementation details.
Does not establish legal compliance or child-data standards; qualified owners must approve applicable requirements.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Open-Day Campaign
use_cases.description: Draft invitations and reminders while separating guardians, prospective learners, and enrolled students and identifying consent or date problems.

use_cases.title: Map a Course Inquiry Journey
use_cases.description: Specify prospectus delivery and optional promotional follow-up with permission checks, enrollment exits, and delayed-send reconciliation.

use_cases.title: Review Recruitment Measurement
use_cases.description: Define inquiry and enrollment reporting with authorized data, comparable intake windows, unique-person denominators, and explicit attribution limits.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Program Introduction
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an introductory email for [program] aimed at [adult audience]. Use these approved facts: [facts]. Include a subject, preheader, body, and one CTA. Mark unknown URLs or claims with placeholders. Do not send.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: create one email from approved program information.

prompt_templates.title: Define Capture and Audience Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan inquiry capture for [program] and [intake] on [platform]. Available fields are [fields]; permission rules are [approved rules]. Define minimal fields, audience segments, guardian separation, and exclusions. Identify missing facts without collecting personal data.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: structure an inquiry form and eligible marketing audience.

prompt_templates.title: Specify an Enrollment-Aware Journey
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a prospectus delivery and follow-up journey for [program]. Use [authoritative status source], [consent rules], and [timezone]. Specify entries, delays, branches, exits, re-entry, deduplication, and retry reconciliation. Recheck permission and enrollment before delayed marketing. Produce a plan only.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: define automation behavior before authorized implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Launch and Measurement Risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this campaign plan: [plan]. Context includes [age ranges], [guardian mapping], [status freshness], [permission evidence], and [approved event facts]. Prioritize blockers, sync failures, shared-email disclosure risks, and uncertain delivery outcomes. Define authorized metrics, comparable intake windows, assumptions, and the next authorized action. Do not modify live systems.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: assess a mixed-audience campaign and its measurement plan.

output_examples.input: Plan an open-day reminder for parents, 15-year-olds, and enrolled students. Consent records are missing, and the event date is last year.
output: Launch status: Hold. Confirm the current event date, timezone, and approved invitation audience.
Permission: Verify marketing consent and the approved process for minors before capture, sharing, or promotional delivery.
Audience: Separate guardian and learner records. Exclude enrolled learners from prospect recruitment where irrelevant.
Next action: Prepare draft copy with date and link placeholders for review. Do not upload contacts or schedule messages.

output_examples.input: Draft an adult course introduction. Approved facts: evening classes, online delivery, and a public information session. The registration URL is unknown.
output: Subject: Explore our evening online course
Preheader: Join a public information session about the program.
Body: Considering evening study? Our online course offers evening classes. Join the information session to learn about the program.
Primary CTA: Register for the information session at [approved registration URL].
Review note: Confirm the session date, timezone, registration destination, and recipient marketing eligibility before launch.

output_examples.input: Plan prospectus delivery with a promotional follow-up three days later. Enrollment status comes from the approved learning system.
output: Entry: A verified prospectus request triggers the promised document delivery.
Follow-up: After three days in the approved timezone, recheck promotional permission, suppression, and authoritative enrollment status.
Exit: Exclude enrolled or withdrawn contacts from recruitment follow-up where relevant.
Failure handling: Hold affected actions when enrollment updates are unresolved. Reconcile delivery logs before retrying a timed-out send.
Execution boundary: This is a specification, not authorization to send or change records.

best_practices: Provide approved program facts, intake dates, timezones, audience age ranges, and authoritative enrollment sources before planning.
Keep marketing permission separate from program interest, guardian identity, requested information delivery, and operational notices.
Review live exclusions, status freshness, recipient mapping, and launch authorization before any upload, schedule, or send.
anti_patterns: Treating every institutional contact or prospectus request as permission for promotional email.
Inferring sensitive traits, collecting unnecessary student records, or promising admission, salary, visa, or qualification outcomes.
Resending after a timeout without checking delivery status, or treating a draft request as permission to launch.

faq.question: Who is this skill for?
faq.answer: It supports schools, training providers, and course teams planning education marketing and informational email journeys.

faq.question: Does it send emails or access accounts automatically?
faq.answer: No bundled sending integration is included. The instructions require applicable authorization for sending, scheduling, uploading personal data, or changing live systems.

faq.question: Can it work with my existing email platform?
faq.answer: It directs the assistant to use your selected platform. Verify current features, personalization syntax, integrations, and plan limits before implementation.

faq.question: Is Poptin required?
faq.answer: No. Poptin is an optional consideration for relevant capture workflows; another platform is explicitly acceptable, and migration is not implied.

faq.question: Can it plan campaigns involving minors?
faq.answer: It identifies age and guardian safeguards, but requires an approved age-appropriate consent process. It does not determine the applicable legal standard.

faq.question: Can it make admissions decisions or guarantee enrollment results?
faq.answer: No. It separates marketing from admissions authority and prohibits guarantees about admission, qualifications, employment, salary, or visa outcomes.
